key_insight: SILSA changes high-resolution 3D generation from many fragmented local voxels to compact sliding-window slice latents, helping preserve continuous surfaces and topology. This makes it better suited for thin, connected, or delicate shapes that are often broken by patch-based methods.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the cost and topological errors in existing 3D generation pipelines that first predict active structure and then synthesize local geometry. These approaches can be expensive at high resolution and may fragment surfaces or fail to keep thin structures connected.
method: Represents shapes using compact sliding-window slice latents instead of many local voxel tokens.
Uses a topology-aware generation strategy to maintain continuity across neighboring slices.
Targets high-resolution 3D synthesis while reducing fragmentation and improving consistency for complex shapes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SILSA offers a more efficient way to generate detailed 3D objects without sacrificing surface continuity. This can improve results in applications like asset creation, simulation, robotics, and digital twins where topology matters.

paper_title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
paper_authors: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Ying Shen, Kiet A. Nguyen
